sections.content: How many people are "agricultural and fishing trades (other)"?

26,430 people

were counted on the census as "agricultural and fishing trades (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work may perform a variety of agricultural, practical conservation activities, and fishing tasks not elsewhere classified.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "agricultural and fishing trades (other)" there were more men than women (92.7% compared with 7.3%).

This means "agricultural and fishing trades (other)" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled agricultural and related trades".

Men made up 92.7% and women made up 7.3% of "agricultural and fishing trades (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "agricultural and fishing trades (other)" included:

  • skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades supervisors
  • IT network professionals
  • marine and waterways transport operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "agricultural and fishing trades (other)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "agricultural and fishing trades (other)", 15.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "agricultural and fishing trades (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

  • data entry administrators
  • air-conditioning and refrigeration installers and repairers
  • groundworkers

We can look at who worked as "agricultural and fishing trades (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "agricultural and fishing trades (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "agricultural and fishing trades (other)", 8.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (82.6% compared with 17.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (52.9%) than self-employed (47.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
